To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exceptional wet integrity of transparent CNF assemblies can be explained by a network model, that the aspect ratio, charge density, and bivalency of the CNFs, as well as the valency of the counter‐ions influence the wet integrity of CNF assemblies, and that these findings can be used in the rational design of CNF assemblies for applications where wet strength is important.
the aspect ratios of the CNFs and the charge density of the CNFs are the main factors influencing the wet integrity of the films.

the exceptional wet integrity of transparent cellulose nanofibril films in the presence of ions is due to the synergistic action of ion–ion correlation (induced by multivalent ions) and specific ion effects (induced by ions with a high charge density).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of cellulose materials for biointerface applications.
the exceptional wet integrity of cellulose nanofibril films in the presence of ions and how this can be used to create suitable substrates for biointerfaces.
the development of transparent, flexible and biocompatible materials based on cellulose nanofibril films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wet modulus of the CNF films is determined by the solidity of the CNF network, which is influenced by the charge density of the CNFs and the counter‐ions, and the aspect ratio of CNFs.
the exceptional wet integrity of CNF films in the presence of counter‐ions can be attributed to a combination of ion–ion correlation, specific ion effects, and the aspect ratio of CNF.

the exceptional wet integrity and strength of TEMPO‐oxidized CNF films in the presence of divalent ions is a result of the combined effects of ion–ion correlation, specific ion effects, and the high aspect ratio of the fibrils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exceptional wet integrity of TEMPO‐oxidized, phosphorylated CNF films in the presence of divalent counter‐ions is due to ion–ion correlation, which is enhanced by specific ion effects.
CNFs are excellent building blocks for wet materials with high wet integrity, and that these materials are suitable for biointerfaces.
we have developed a new class of transparent, wet‐strength materials with a tunable wet modulus, and that we have identified the essential factors behind this behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNFs can be used to make wet materials with high wet strength, which is a prerequisite for a wide range of applications, including biointerfaces.
the wet strength of transparent CNF films can be tuned by the charge density and valency of the counter‐ions.
a combination of ion–ion correlation, specific ion effects, and the aspect ratio of CNFs is essential for the formation of wet resilient films with high strength and ductility.
